subject: Model fit & function-calling evals — next steps and benchmark links
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: model fit / function-calling evals + next steps

Hi Sarah — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: generate structured order confirmations (JSON) from unstructured customer emails and chat logs.
- Success metrics: >=95% schema compliance on critical fields (order_id, sku, qty, price), avg latency <350ms for 1-2 token responses in our staging layout, and low regression vs your current rules pipeline.
- Data: you shared a sample set (~2k messages) and a target JSON schema. Thanks for that — attaching an example prompt set and schema for reference.

Proposed technical eval plan:
1) Model fit: run A/B on 3 model variants (low-latency small, mid-size accuracy, quantized large for cost):
   - redwood/opt-1.3b (fast)
   - open-mpt-7b-instruct (mid)
   - redwood/quant-llama-13b (cost/quality sweet spot)
2) Function-calling / structured output: evaluate JSON schema compliance, validation errors, and automated retries for malformed responses.
3) Benchmarks: run on a holdout of 500 examples, produce per-field precision/recall, schema pass rate, and end-to-end latency.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.json, acme_output_schema.json (please confirm these match what you intended).

Questions for you before we run the evals:
- Confirm the target schema above is final (any optional fields we should ignore for pass/fail?).
- Are any PII/redaction rules we need to apply before sending data to hosted evals?
- Preferred time for a 45-min technical run-through next week (we can include Marissa and Neha).

Next steps (if you confirm): we’ll provision a dedicated staging run, share benchmark results in ~3 business days, and sync to review tradeoffs (quality vs cost).

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

Thanks Rishi — this is great, and the plan looks aligned. A few quick notes: 

- Schema: the attached acme_output_schema.json is the one we use in production, but please ignore the optional "campaign_code" field for pass/fail. Everything else should be strict.
- PII: strip email addresses and payment tokens before sending; we can provide a scrubbed subset (I'll attach).
- Attachments: I’ve attached acme_prompt_set_v1.json (sample prompts) and acme_output_schema.json. Also sending a small benchmark CSV (acme_benchmark_sample.csv) for quick sanity checks.

Regarding retries: our current rules pipeline will do up to 2 corrective passes if the schema validator fails (try reorganize fields / infer missing ids). If you can simulate a similar retry policy in the evals, that’d help us compare apples-to-apples.

We’re good for a 45-min session next Wednesday 2/18 at 10:00am PT. Can you send a calendar invite?

— Sarah

Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit / function-calling evals + next steps

Thanks for pulling this together Rishi. A few technical recommendations from the model/ops side that will shape the eval: 

1) Function-calling JSON compliance:
   - Use strict schema validation (jsonschema) for pass/fail. Report both hard fails (invalid JSON) and soft fails (missing required keys).
   - For malformed JSON responses, capture the raw tokens and the parser error to help prompt-tune.

2) Retry policy to mimic production: 
   - Retry 1: prompt augmentation — include the last parse error and an explicit example of expected output.
   - Retry 2: fallback to a smaller deterministic model with a templated output shim (better at consistent formatting).
   - If still failing, mark as "requires human review". We'll report triage cost rate.

3) Metrics to export per-run:
   - Schema pass rate (primary), field-level F1 scores for order_id/sku/qty/price, avg tokens per response, 95th latency, and cost per 1k examples.

4) Instrumentation: add a per-request validation trace (validator status, retry count, model variant) so you can slice by error mode in Redwood Console.

I’ll prepare a short eval playbook for the run so Sarah can follow the remediation steps for failures.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
